keyword_results.evidence: Two curved stitched panel lines are visible on the teal bodice from the upper bodice beside the neckline, over the bust, to the fitted waist seam. Their relief/stitched continuity belongs to the dress, rather than a print.

Both sleeves have pronounced gathered shoulder and upper-arm volume, tapering into close-fitting elbow-to-wrist lower sleeves and cuffs attached to the same dress.
Both hip pocket mouths are narrow horizontal dark slits framed by slim matching fabric lips. They are inset into the skirt/dress, remain clear of hands, and do not read as patch or flap pockets.

Ivory edging follows the neckline and both cuff boundaries, but at native scale the visible trim reads as a narrow light band. Its raised cord-like cross-section is not distinguishable confidently from flat binding. The required dimensional relation is unconfirmed.

keyword_results.evidence: Two outer front-skirt fold edges turn toward the center and meet at the upper stitched front section; below them a darker recessed underfold is exposed between the edges. The center is recessed rather than a projecting box panel or open bare slit.

A small silver connector is present above the rectangular pendant and the necklace descends toward it. The connector spans only a few native pixels; a separate open bail and the chain passing through its opening cannot be resolved. A top connection alone does not prove the specified bail topology.

Both black shoe uppers remain in frame. On the forward shoe, separate eyelet-bearing quarters visibly sit above the vamp with open V edges surrounding the tongue and laces; the rear shoe also shows open lacing.

keyword_results.evidence: The ochre pullover has a collarless round neck and a visible short center-front button placket that terminates within the front body.

Raised crossed and braided yarn columns repeat over the ochre torso panel; they have local relief and are not a flat rope print.
